02 / FULL-RANGE CORRELATION

Co-movement, at a glance.

−1: opposite directions · 0: no linear relationship · +1: same direction

03 / INTERPRETING THE EVIDENCE

A correlation is not a verdict.

Low average correlation can suggest diversification potential. It does not establish protection in a crisis.

A safe-haven claim needs a defined stress benchmark, sufficient extreme observations, uncertainty estimates and out-of-sample checks. This explorer provides descriptive evidence, not that classification.

01 / YOUR DATA

Bring your own evidence.

Upload one aligned CSV with the columns below. Files stay in this browser session.

date,bitcoin,gold,dxy

ISO dates (YYYY-MM-DD). Positive prices. Blank asset values drop that date; duplicate dates and invalid prices reject the file. Use compatible USD series and document the exact proxies.

02 / PROVENANCE

Know what you are looking at.

Gold futures are a proxy, not physical gold or a spot-gold investment. Futures roll effects and close-time differences can affect comparisons. DXY is an index, not a directly investable portfolio.
03 / METHODS

Simple calculations. Explicit assumptions.

01

Align observed dates

Keep only dates with positive observations for all three assets. Never create weekend prices by forward-filling. No exchange-calendar completeness claim is made.

02

Use log returns consistently

rₜ = ln(Pₜ) − ln(Pₜ₋₁). Both full-range and rolling correlations use these returns. Volatility is the sample standard deviation, with divisor n − 1.

03

Keep the full risk picture

Extreme returns stay in the sample. Drawdown uses the running peak inside the selected range. Undefined correlations are shown as unavailable, not zero.

04

Make findings reproducible

Exports include the selected prices, source note, period, formulas and computed statistics. The R pipeline saves raw source rows and package versions; fixed dates alone do not freeze a vendor’s data.

Implemented: descriptive statistics, normalised prices, drawdowns, Pearson correlations, rolling correlations and conditional DXY-tail analysis.
Not implemented: DCC-GARCH, Markov-switching, causality models, ETF-flow analysis, portfolio optimisation or predictive safe-haven signals.
